stages.does: Pulsed near-infrared light; two photons are absorbed together only where the light is densest, at the focus.
Sets how much excitation reaches the sample (transmission %), and whether it rises with depth (Bright Z on Olympus/Evident).

symptoms.explanation: Tissue scatters the excitation, so fewer photons arrive at the focus the deeper it is; two-photon signal grows with the square of the excitation, so the loss compounds; the emitted light is scattered on its way back too. Power that rises with depth compensates.
symptoms.check: Acquired data: brightest 1 % by depth falling; Light path: Bright Z off or a flat ramp.
symptoms.alternatives: Fewer labelled cells deeper (biology), or a tilted or uneven sample.

symptoms.symptom: Top planes clip while deep planes stay dim.
symptoms.explanation: The ramp starts too high or the detector gain is set for the deep planes: one setting cannot suit both ends of the stack.
symptoms.check: Acquired data: clipped voxels in the first planes only; brightest 1 % low at depth.
symptoms.alternatives: A bright structure that only sits near the surface (capsule, SHG collagen).

symptoms.symptom: Background rises with depth at high power.
symptoms.explanation: At high power, fluorescence excited away from the focus (near the surface) adds a haze that sets the depth limit.
symptoms.check: Acquired data: median by depth rising while the brightest 1 % does not.

stages.does: Moves the focus across the field. Zoom sets the pixel size; dwell time sets photons per pixel; resonant scanners trade dwell for speed.

symptoms.symptom: Pixel size or z-step coarser than the optical resolution.
symptoms.explanation: Detail finer than two pixels is not recorded. Whether that matters depends on the question: coarse sampling is normal for tracking cells, a problem for morphology.
symptoms.check: Light path: pixel size, z-step, objective NA. Ask the user's question before calling it a mistake.
symptoms.alternatives: A deliberate trade for speed, field size or less light dose.

stages.does: Focuses the excitation and collects the emission; NA sets resolution and light collection; the correction collar matters for depth in water.
Scatters and absorbs light, bleaches, and can be damaged by the light.

symptoms.explanation: Photobleaching at the focus rises faster than the signal as power goes up, so a power that gives a bright first frame can bleach quickly. Photodamage also rises steeply with power.
symptoms.check: Acquired data: brightest 1 % by frame falling; Light path: power and frame interval.
symptoms.alternatives: Cells leaving the field, drift in z, a change in the animal (biology). Bleaching is only one candidate.

stages.does: Dichroics and emission filters split the emission between detectors.

symptoms.symptom: One structure shows up in two channels.
symptoms.explanation: Bleed-through (emission spilling into a neighbouring channel) or cross-excitation (one laser exciting two dyes). Filters are often not recorded in the file, so it has to be measured.
symptoms.check: Light path: channels sharing a laser; the file's filters (often not recorded).
symptoms.alternatives: Real co-labelling of the same cells.

stages.does: Turn photons into a signal; HV/gain amplify it, offset shifts it.

symptoms.symptom: Bright structures clip at the top of the range.
symptoms.explanation: Gain (HV) or power too high: values above the ceiling are lost and cannot be recovered in analysis.
symptoms.check: Acquired data: clipped at a detected ceiling, share of signal clipped.
symptoms.alternatives: None for the clipped voxels; how much it matters depends on whether they are the cells being measured.

symptoms.symptom: Most of the background is exactly 0.
symptoms.explanation: Offset set so the background is cut off at 0: dim signal near the background is lost and the noise floor cannot be measured.
symptoms.check: Acquired data: % of voxels at 0; noise floor 'not measurable: background clipped at 0'.
symptoms.alternatives: Background subtracted after acquisition (upstream processing) looks the same.

stages.does: Turns the signal into numbers; frames can be averaged or summed.

symptoms.symptom: Values above what one detector read can give.
symptoms.explanation: Summing frames adds them, so the range doubles per extra frame; averaging keeps the range and lowers noise.
symptoms.check: Light path: integration sum/average and count.
symptoms.alternatives: Background added in processing, or a different store format.

stages.does: Repeats the frame over z and time: z-step, plane count, frame interval.

features.name: Bright Z
features.line: Bright Z: set laser power at the top and at the bottom of the stack; it is interpolated in between.

features.name: Auto HV
features.line: Auto HV: the software sets detector HV; the file may then record HV 0, so judge gain from the measured clipping.

features.name: Bright Z
features.line: Bright Z: set laser power at several depths of the stack; check that it is switched on, not only set.
